answers.asked: US patient with eGFR 32?, then
answers.answer:
If the eGFR is 32 mL/min, it falls in the label’s ≥30 mL/min category. For an adult with chronic HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), the labeled starting dose is 20 mg once daily, with a target of 40 mg once daily after 4 weeks; monitor serum potassium and blood pressure. [cardionex-uspi-v2, 2.2]

If “32?” means the eGFR is uncertain or may be below 30, confirm the value before applying the dose recommendation—the label gives a different regimen below 30. [cardionex-uspi-v2, 2.2]

retrieved.title: Worsening Renal Function
retrieved.text: Serum creatinine may rise in the first weeks of treatment. Measure creatinine at baseline and after 1 to 2 weeks. A rise of more than 30% from baseline calls for a review of the diuretic dose and of other drugs that affect the kidneys.

retrieved.title: Hepatic Impairment
retrieved.text: No dose change is needed in mild or moderate hepatic impairment (ChildPugh A or B). CardioNex has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and is not recommended there.

answers.asked: What happened to potassium in the CLARION-HF trial?
answers.answer: In CLARION-HF, mean serum potassium increased by 0.3 mEq/L by week 4 and then remained level. Potassium above 5.5 mEq/L occurred in 4.1% of CardioNex-treated patients versus 1.9% on placebo; among patients also taking spironolactone, it occurred in 7.6%. [cardioNex-clarion-hf-trial, 3.4]

retrieved.title: Adverse Reactions and Initiation Thresholds
retrieved.text:
- Common Adverse Events (CardioNex vs. Placebo): Symptomatic hypotension (9.1% vs. 4.5%), hyperkalemia (6.8% vs. 3.4%), worsening renal function (4.2% vs. 3.8%), angioedema (0.4% vs. 0.1%).

- Footnote † (Potassium Exclusion Rule): Patients with screening serum potassium > 5.2 mEq/L were excluded from CLARION-HF. Per clinical

protocol and labeling, do NOT initiate CardioNex if baseline serum potassium exceeds 5.0 mEq/L.

retrieved.title: Potassium and Kidney Results
retrieved.text:
- Mean serum potassium rose by 0.3 mEq/L by week 4 and then stayed level.

- Serum potassium above 5.5 mEq/ L at any visit: 4.1% on CardioNex and 1.9% on placebo.

- Patients also taking spironolactone had potassium above 5.5 mEq/L in 7.6% of cases.

- Mean eGFR fell by 3 mL/min in the first month and did not fall further.

retrieved.title: Indications and Usage
retrieved.text:
CardioNex is indicated ONLY to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF <= 40%).

- Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in pediatric patients (< 18 years).

- Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF > 40%).

retrieved.title: Boxed Warning and Contraindications
retrieved.text:
- BOXED WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue CardioNex as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the reninangiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

CONTRAINDICATIONS:

- Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors is contraindicated due to angioedema risk. Allow a strict 36-hour washout period when switching from an ACE inhibitor to CardioNex.

- Contraindicated in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring dialysis.

| Patient Population | Recommended Starting Dose | Target Maintenance Dose | Notes & Exceptions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Standard Adult HFrEF (eGFR >= 30 mL/min) | 20mg once daily | 40mg once daily (titrate after 4 weeks) | Monitor serum potassium and blood pressure |
| Severe Renal Impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min, non-dialysis) | 5mg once daily | 5mg once daily | Do not titrate above 5mg |
| End-Stage Renal Disease (on dialysis) | Contraindicated | Contraindicated | Do not administer |
| Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors* | 5mg once daily | 5mg once daily | Applies regardless of renal function |

**Footnote \*:** In patients concurrently taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, or ritonavir), the maximum daily dose of CardioNex **must NOT exceed 5mg once daily**, even if renal function is normal (eGFR >= 30 mL/min).
